animal_proteins.title: Animal proteins
animal_proteins.description: Animal protein allergy: a reaction to proteins found in meat, dairy, eggs, and fish, which may cause skin and digestive symptoms.

cereals_and_gluten.title: Cereals and gluten
cereals_and_gluten.description: Cereals and gluten allergy: sensitivity to proteins in wheat, barley, and rye, affecting breads, pastas, and baked goods.

pulses_and_seeds.title: Pulses and seeds
pulses_and_seeds.description: Pulses and seeds allergy: an adverse reaction to legumes and seeds (e.g., peas, lentils, beans, sesame), potentially leading to digestive issues.

dried_nuts.title: Dried nuts
dried_nuts.description: Dried nuts allergy: sensitivity to tree nuts like walnuts, almonds, and hazelnuts, with a risk of severe reactions such as anaphylaxis.

fruit_and_vegetables.title: Fruit and vegetables
fruit_and_vegetables.description: Fruit and vegetables allergy: an allergic reaction to proteins in various fruits and vegetables (such as strawberries, tomatoes, bell peppers), which may cause irritation or itching.

spices_and_condiments.title: Spices and condiments
spices_and_condiments.description: Spices and condiments allergy: hypersensitivity to common seasonings like pepper, paprika, or turmeric, potentially affecting digestion or causing irritation.

gluten_intolerance.title: Gluten intolerance
gluten_intolerance.description: Gluten intolerance: difficulty digesting gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye, leading to bloating and diarrhea.

lactose_intolerance.title: Lactose intolerance
lactose_intolerance.description: Lactose intolerance: inability to digest lactose in dairy products, resulting in abdominal pain and bloating.

sorbitol_intolerance.title: Sorbitol intolerance
sorbitol_intolerance.description: Sorbitol intolerance: poor absorption of the natural sugar sorbitol, found in some fruits and as a sweetener, which can cause digestive discomfort.

soy_intolerance.title: Soy intolerance
soy_intolerance.description: Soy intolerance: digestive issues triggered by soy products such as tofu or soy milk, causing gastrointestinal discomfort.

histamine_intolerance.title: Histamine intolerance
histamine_intolerance.description: Histamine intolerance: inability to break down histamine present in fermented or aged foods (like cheeses, wines, sausages), leading to headaches and flushing.

fructose_intolerance.title: Fructose intolerance
fructose_intolerance.description: Fructose intolerance: difficulty absorbing fructose found in fruits, some vegetables, and honey, which may result in bloating and diarrhea.

diabetes.title: Diabetes (Type 1 or Type 2)
diabetes.description: Diabetes (Type 1 or Type 2): a condition affecting blood sugar regulation, requiring careful management of carbohydrate and sugar intake.

hypertension.title: Hypertension
hypertension.description: Hypertension: high blood pressure that necessitates limiting salt and saturated fat intake, especially from processed foods.

celiac_disease.title: Celiac disease
celiac_disease.description: Celiac disease: an autoimmune reaction to gluten found in wheat, barley, and rye. A strict gluten-free diet is essential to prevent intestinal damage.

sodium_and_saturated_fat_reduction.title: Sodium and saturated fat reduction
sodium_and_saturated_fat_reduction.description: Sodium and saturated fat reduction: reducing processed foods, salt, and animal fats to support cardiovascular health.

low_fodmap_diet.title: Low FODMAP diet
low_fodmap_diet.description: Low FODMAP diet: a dietary approach that limits certain fermentable carbohydrates (e.g., garlic, onions, some fruits, dairy) to alleviate digestive symptoms.

added_sugar_reduction.title: Added sugar reduction
added_sugar_reduction.description: Added sugar reduction: decreasing consumption of sugary drinks and processed foods for better energy management and overall health.

nutri_grade.description: Nutri-Grade “grades” your drinks based on their sugar and saturated fat content with “A” having the lowest levels and “D” the highest.

eco_grade.question: Do you care about the Eco-Grade ?
eco_grade.description: Eco-grade means the plant is Economy Grade or less than perfect.
